title: American Airlines 1
summary: American Airlines Flight 1 rolled over and crashed into Jamaica Bay two minutes after taking off from Idlewild Airport on 1 March 1962, killing all 87 passengers and eight crew aboard. During a left turn to 290 degrees at 1,600 ft, the Boeing 707 banked too sharply, rolled past 90 degrees, and entered a nearly vertical, upside-down dive before striking Pumpkin Patch Channel. The CAB traced the cause to a short circuit in wires damaged during manufacturing at a Bendix plant, producing a rudder malfunction that led to a loss of control from which the crew could not recover.

The aircraft had an unusually long takeoff run, climbed slowly, struggled to gain lift, and struck trees in darkness. title: 1962 Turkish Airlines Taurus Mountains crash

While descending through cumulus clouds at 6800 feet, the aircraft impacted Mount Medetsiz. title: Flying Tiger Line 923
summary: A Lockheed Constellation L-1049H ditched in the North Atlantic on September 23, 1962 while attempting to divert to Shannon, Ireland. Engine 3 fire warning sounded at 20:19 GMT and the engine was shut down. title: United Airlines 297
summary: A Vickers Viscount 745D was cleared to descend from 10,000 to 6,000 feet during a scheduled flight from Newark to Atlanta. At 12:19 p.m. controllers advised the crew of numerous reports of large numbers of ducks and geese in the area. At 6,000 feet the aircraft struck two whistling swans with its stabilizers. The loss of the left stabilizer caused immediate loss of control; the aircraft's altitude dropped to ground level in less than a minute. title: 1962 LOT Vickers Viscount Warsaw crash
summary: A Vickers Viscount crashed during landing approach in dense fog near Warsaw. The captain, accustomed to piston-engine aircraft, executed a rapid throttle increase inappropriate for turboprop engines, resulting in a stall at low speed. All 33 occupants were killed.
probable_cause: Crew error due to inadequate training on turboprop engine characteristics.

factors.evidence: The captain was accustomed to flying piston engine aircraft in which such maneuvers are allowed
probable causes of the stalling due to low speed
dense near-ground fog, 6/8 overcast, fractostratus clouds at 250 meters
sudden throttle increase is not recommended for turboprop engines but likely executed by the captain

events.text: While on approach on runway 33 in Warsaw the crew received landing clearance.
A sudden throttle increase likely executed by the captain, which is not recommended for turboprop engines.
The plane crashed and burned 1335 meters from the threshold in harsh winter weather with dense near-ground fog.

title: 1962 Air Nautic Boeing 307 crash

agencies.name: Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety

summary: A 22-year-old Boeing 307 on a charter flight made insufficient preparation for the flight and committed serious navigation errors, incorrectly estimating the aircraft's position. The crew failed to maintain the cruising altitude from the flight plan, did not properly monitor navigation, and descended prematurely, entering instrument conditions before striking Monte Renoso mountain with all 25 occupants killed.
probable_cause: Crew failed to follow flight plan cruising altitude, made errors in position estimation, and descended below safe altitude for terrain.

factors.evidence: crew failed to observe the cruising altitude entered on the flight plan and check properly the navigation of the aircraft, which resulted in a wrong estimation of the position of the aircraft
they failed to maintain a safe altitude and started the descent prematurely
a series of errors had been made by the crew, who made insufficient preparation for the flight and committed a serious error in estimating the duration of the flight
crashed into Monte Renoso mountain

events.text: Aircraft cruising at altitude dictated by flight plan but crew failed to observe this altitude correctly
